title: {name} Enterprise

pilot.title: A pilot in an afternoon
pilot.steps: Take a release signed by Warehouse SAS, or build one, and serve it from IIS, Azure Static Web Apps, S3, a container or any static host.
One policy.json beside index.html names your brains, your rules and every address {name} may use.
The browser then refuses every other address, whatever {name}’s own settings say.
Open policy.html at your address. It reads your policy and headers, tries each address, and says what’s wrong.
pilot.after: Then people open the address, sign in with their work account and start. Edge and Chrome can install it as an app through Intune.
pilot.kit: The pilot kit: the recipes, the policy, the header set and the trust pack
people.title: One box, for everyone
people.body: A question, a file or a folder goes in; back comes an answer with its sources, a Word document, a spreadsheet, a deck or a chart. Numbers are worked out by code, not guessed. In 33 languages, right to left included. It asks before sending, sharing or deleting anything.
people.ask: Turn this into a one-page summary for the board.
people.answer: Sales grew 12% on the quarter, led by the north. The summary and a chart are in Q3 summary.docx.
answers.title: What your teams will ask
answers.why: One line per question, with its status today. The documents to attach to your review are in the trust pack.
answers.security: Where do prompts and files go?
To your gateway and nowhere else. Your header makes the browser enforce it.
built
What can code the AI writes reach?
It runs in a sandboxed worker with an opaque origin and no network. The page enforces Trusted Types and a strict policy.
built
What stays on laptops?
Each person’s work, sealed with AES-256-GCM. Policy can require a passkey or password lock.
built
Is every action logged?
Each turn, brain call and tool use goes to your OpenTelemetry collector. Your gateway’s log stays the authoritative one.
key
How do we trust a release?
Releases are signed and come with a CycloneDX bill of materials, checked with OpenSSH. Three libraries load up front.
built
Does it follow ANSSI’s guide?
Each of its 35 recommendations for generative AI systems is mapped in the trust pack: what {name} does, what is left to you, what isn’t built.
built
Has it been tested from outside?
The brief for the test is published. The test isn’t done yet.
not
answers.privacy: Not for your deployment: nothing of yours passes through our servers.
A template, filled in for what {name} does and left blank for what you decide.
Can we keep records for a set time?
Each task is kept at least as long as you set, six months for the AI Act, with its certificates.
Pictures and files {name} makes are marked, and each answer has a certificate saying where it was done.
Is our data used to train models?
We never receive it. The terms of your gateway’s providers apply.

Nothing reaches us. Your audit is off unless you turn it on.
Metadata only by default: which brain, which tool, when. Content only if you add it.
When the audit is on, yes, by their work address. Your agreement with staff representatives decides.

MCP connections that sign in from the browser, named or denied by policy.

faq.title: Questions
faq.items: Can it sit alongside Microsoft 365 Copilot?
Yes. It serves the people without a Copilot licence, on any device with a browser, and reads and writes Microsoft 365 through your own app registration.
Can it run without the internet?
With your gateway on premises and the header limited to it, nothing leaves your network. On a capable computer, {name} can also answer on the device.
Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint: LiteLLM, Portkey, Cloudflare AI Gateway, Azure API Management, and public services such as Albert or GWDG’s SAIA.
Can we put our name on it?
Yes: your name and colours, and your own privacy page and terms.
You keep the releases and the code under MIT, and people keep their files. If no key can be bought for 12 months, the enterprise code becomes MIT.
